---
title: "Hypothesis Test for Population Mean Difference"
format: html
editor: visual
self-contained: true
---

## Question 1 (4 points)

A music researcher wants to determine whether noise-canceling headphones improve focus while listening to music. The researcher conducts an experiment where 30 participants complete a concentration task, first without noise-canceling headphones and then again with them. They record the number of tasks they complete in each condition and look at the differences (with headphones minus without headphones). Here we assume an improvement means they can complete more tasks. They find the mean difference to be 0.8 with a sample standard deviation of 2.

In the code block below, perform a hypothesis test at the 5% significance level to test these claims. STATE YOUR CONCLUSION IN CONTEXT OF THE PROBLEM.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
alpha <- 0.05
xbard <- 0.8
s <- 2
n <- 30

cat("Test Statistic: ", xbard/(s/sqrt(n)), "\n")
cat("Critical Value: ", qt(1-alpha, n-1), "\n")
cat("P-Value: ", 1-pt(xbard/(s/sqrt(n)), n-1), "\n")
```

[With a p-value of $0.0183 < 0.05$, we reject the null hypothesis and conclude that the mean difference of the number of tasks completed is significantly greater than 0.]{style="color: red;"}

## Question 2 (4 points)

A medical researcher is testing the effect of a new drug on reducing blood sugar levels in diabetic patients. The researcher collects data from 60 participants with Type 2 diabetes, measuring their blood sugar levels (in mg/dL) before starting the drug (baseline) and again after 12 weeks of treatment. The goal is to determine whether the drug significantly reduces blood sugar levels in these patients. The data are found below:

```{r, echo = TRUE}
before <- c(106, 105, 102, 108, 100, 103, 98, 100, 97, 103, 99, 96, 96, 96, 93,
            98, 99, 98, 101, 99, 99, 94, 98, 94, 97, 102, 100, 100, 102, 104,
            104, 106, 101, 102, 97, 101, 101, 99, 103, 97, 93, 99, 92, 107, 108,
            107, 97, 107, 107, 95, 101, 102, 105, 98, 102, 105, 91, 93, 96, 100)

after <- c(102, 100, 101, 99, 98, 97, 96, 96, 98, 96, 103, 95, 97, 97, 98, 100,
           99, 100, 96, 97, 99, 96, 98, 100, 93, 105, 96, 95, 100, 101, 107,
           106, 101, 97, 96, 101, 101, 97, 106, 99, 86, 101, 90, 103, 99, 106,
           100, 101, 101, 93, 97, 98, 100, 98, 98, 99, 102, 101, 95, 103)
```

In the code block below, perform a hypothesis test at the 5% significance level to test these claims. STATE YOUR CONCLUSION IN CONTEXT OF THE PROBLEM.

```{r, echo = TRUE}
t.test(after, before, alternative = "less", paired = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)
```

[With a p-value of $0.01078 < 0.05$, we reject the null hypothesis and conclude that the mean difference in blood pressure is significantly less than 0.]{style="color: red;"}
